title: Denver Trivia Night

questions.q: An engraved step on the west side of the Colorado State Capitol marks what famous measurement?
Denver was founded in 1858 where Cherry Creek meets which river?
Which Major League Baseball team plays at Coors Field?
The Denver Nuggets won their first NBA championship in which year?
Which quarterback led the Denver Broncos to back-to-back Super Bowl wins in the late 1990s?
What is the name of the famous open-air music venue set among giant sandstone formations just west of Denver?
Denver socialite Margaret "Molly" Brown became famous for surviving which 1912 disaster?
The giant blue mustang statue with glowing red eyes outside Denver International Airport has what nickname?
Coins struck at the Denver Mint carry which single-letter mint mark?
The city was named after James W. Denver, a governor of which territory?

notes: The 13th step of the Capitol's west steps is engraved 'One Mile Above Sea Level'; see Colorado State Capitol (Wikipedia).
Founded 1858 at the confluence of Cherry Creek and the South Platte River; see Denver and South Platte River (Wikipedia).
Coors Field, home of the Colorado Rockies since 1995; see Coors Field (Wikipedia) or MLB.com.
Nuggets beat the Miami Heat in the 2023 NBA Finals for their first title; see 2023 NBA Finals (Wikipedia).
Elway won Super Bowls XXXII and XXXIII (1998 and 1999 games); see John Elway (Wikipedia).
Red Rocks Amphitheatre, Morrison, Colorado, owned by the City of Denver; see Red Rocks Amphitheatre (Wikipedia).
Margaret Brown survived the Titanic sinking in April 1912; her Denver home is the Molly Brown House Museum; see Margaret Brown (Wikipedia).
Luis Jimenez's 'Blue Mustang' sculpture at DEN, widely nicknamed Blucifer; see Blue Mustang (Wikipedia).
The Denver Mint uses the 'D' mint mark; see Denver Mint (Wikipedia) or usmint.gov.
Named in 1858 for James W. Denver, governor of Kansas Territory; see Denver (Wikipedia) and James W. Denver (Wikipedia).
